    Proposition 6.1: residual correction spaces (spanning form) #

    prop:residual-correction-spaces and Appendix B: in characteristic two, under the brick hypothesis, "each periodic component contributes at most one correction line, represented by a single path". We record: there is a set S of rows at periodic vertices, at most one in each periodic component, whose classes span all derivative cokernels in degrees at least three (residual_cokerSpan).

    Deviation from the source: the source takes I to be exactly the components with a nonzero class; we keep all components with a candidate row (a superset), which is what the spanning statement needs. The component models and degrees of the rows are recorded by connected_cokerSpan and the files StarDSpan, StarESpan.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

      Proposition 6.1, spanning form (prop:residual-correction-spaces). In characteristic two, for a finite-dimensional scalar mesh category on a finite translation quiver with at most one arrow between ordered vertices, satisfying the brick hypothesis, there is a set of rows at periodic vertices, at most one in each periodic component, whose classes span the cokernels of all D_m, m ≥ 2.
